A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GPDiT, with matching core methods and main experiments. Text, equations, figures and tables are accessible. v1 ends after its references; v5 adds Appendix A.1–A.3, which is included in this comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation measurements, linear-probing results and qualitative few-shot experiments in Tables 2–3 and Figures 4–7.

after.justification: v5 retains those experiments and adds original convergence, visual question answering and style-generalization results in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The core GPDiT architecture, attention variants, diffusion objective and rotation conditioning remain unchanged. Appendix A.2 adds a downstream VQA adaptation: GPDiT-H's first 18 layers replace Video-ChatGPT's CLIP encoder, with a resized trainable linear projection and frozen feature extractor.

E1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds ActivityNet-QA video question answering, extending evaluation beyond generation and action classification. Appendix A.3 adds multiple face-style-to-real mappings and generalization to an unseen target style. Existing datasets and tasks remain represented.

E2.justification: Table 4 introduces Video-ChatGPT as the comparator for the new VQA evaluation. Comparator membership in the existing MSRVTT and UCF-101 comparisons in Tables 2–3 is unchanged.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark protocols remain stable, but the appendix substantially extends evaluation design. VQA trains only the replacement projection for six epochs with batch size 4 and learning rate 2e-5, reporting accuracy and Score. Style experiments introduce explicit disjoint-image and held-out-target-style evaluations, including training on ten styles and testing an unseen style.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained layer, attention and checkpoint analyses in Figure 5, v5 adds OF-versus-OF2 convergence curves, targeted camera-motion case studies, and explicit within-style versus unseen-style generalization tests in Figures 8–11. The held-out-style experiment substantively extends the robustness evidence beyond v1's task demonstrations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for these experiments. Figure 8's new training-loss trajectories do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 and Figure 5 retain their results. New Table 4 reports GPDiT-H-OF2-Long at 28.2% accuracy and 1.54 Score, versus Video-ChatGPT at 35.2% and 2.8. Added convergence curves and style-generalization outputs substantially expand the reported findings; they do not establish improved performance over v1 under existing benchmark settings.

T1.justification: The diffusion SDE and probability-flow ODE, training objective, attention-complexity analysis, and rotation/inverse-rotation derivation in Sections 3–4 retain the same mathematical content. The appendix adds no formal assumptions, propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introductory contributions and concluding claims retain the same scope: autoregressive diffusion video modeling, efficient attention and time conditioning, and generative, representational and few-shot capabilities. The appendix supplies additional evidence without redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly acknowledges resource constraints on scaling and the model's modality limitations. Appendix A interprets VQA transfer without language pretraining and distinguishes within-style from unseen-style generalization. The existing explanations of generation and representation behavior remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 newly specifies that the existing total batch size of 96 is distributed across 32 H100 GPUs. Appendix A supplies the VQA encoder/projection configuration and training hyperparameters, plus style counts, sample counts and training duration. The original GPDiT training recipes remain stable.

R1.justification: v5 adds the Video-ChatGPT paper and uses that system to position the new VQA transfer experiment. The earlier references and substantive related-work discussion are retained after citation renumbering.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are retained. v5 makes localized wording edits, adds an author, renames Conclusion to Discussion, and adds a limitations paragraph and experimental appendix. This does not amount to extensive rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v5 adds Figures 8–11 and Table 4: convergence curves, annotated camera-motion comparisons, style-generalization examples and VQA results. Figure 1 moves to the first page, and several retained figures and tables are resized or repositioned. The original architecture diagram and main result displays remain present.

improvement.justification: Appendix A adds useful convergence, VQA-transfer and held-out-style evidence absent from v1, while hardware disclosure and explicit limitations improve transparency. These gains modestly strengthen the paper. Their impact is limited by largely qualitative camera/style evidence and sparse VQA evaluation details, including an undefined Score metric; the core method and headline results remain unchanged.
